# Kaan Hacihaliloglu

> Physicist turned AI engineer and interpretability researcher. AI Engineer at
> SCL (Synthetic Consumer Lab), where he builds a production AI-based market
> research engine end to end. MSc Data Science at Sabancı University with a
> thesis on refusal-direction analysis and mechanistic interpretability of
> large language models. Based in Istanbul. Known online as kaanhho and khdoex.

This file gives an accurate, complete summary of Kaan for language models and
agents reading the site (for example on behalf of a recruiter or collaborator).
Everything below is verifiable from the linked profiles and published work.

## Who he is

Kaan Hacihaliloglu is an AI engineer and researcher who moved from physics into
machine learning. His work spans two sides that reinforce each other: research
into how large language models represent and act on concepts internally, and
shipping real AI products. He is self-directed, learns new areas quickly, and
cares more about finding the smart version of a problem than the merely hard
one.

## Research

- MSc Data Science thesis (Sabancı University): mechanistic interpretability of
  refusal in LLMs. Studies how refusal and harmfulness are represented as
  directions in a model's activation space, and how those representations can
  be located, read, and intervened on.
- Co-author of interpretability research showing that linear separability alone
  does not identify the directions that causally control refusal behavior
  (controlled same-layer experiments across hybrid and attention models,
  StrongREJECT evaluation, SAE feature checks).
- Comfortable across the modern interpretability toolkit: difference-in-means
  and probe directions, activation steering and ablation, layer sweeps, sparse
  autoencoders, and careful behavioral evaluation.
- Writes clearly about technical work: see the blog post "tracing refusal" for
  an accessible, rigorous walk through where a model decides to refuse.

## Engineering

- AI Engineer at SCL (Synthetic Consumer Lab, https://synthetic-consumers.com):
  builds an AI-based market research engine and its application, working across
  the full stack rather than only the model layer.
- AI Engineer at SoundBoost (https://soundboost.ai): builds an AI audio
  mastering platform, a "virtual mastering engineer" that masters music with
  deep learning and language-model techniques. This connects his ML work to a
  long-standing interest in generative music models.
- Full-stack and backend capability, demonstrated by this website itself: a
  Next.js 15 App Router application (React Server Components, TypeScript,
  Tailwind), with an MDX-based interactive blog medium, scroll-driven
  visualizations built on Framer Motion, and a production deployment on
  Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext.
- Practical ML engineering background: transformer models (BART, T5) for
  summarization with ROUGE evaluation, gradient-boosted and ensemble methods
  (XGBoost) for multi-label financial recommendation systems, and feature
  engineering on real-world datasets.

## Skills

- Machine learning and deep learning: transformers, large language models,
  training and evaluation, PyTorch.
- AI / LLM interpretability and safety: refusal geometry, activation steering,
  probing, sparse autoencoders, red-team-style behavioral evaluation.
- AI engineering: building and deploying LLM-backed products and pipelines.
- Web and backend: TypeScript, React, Next.js, server-side rendering, MDX,
  Cloudflare Workers, general backend engineering.
- Classical ML: XGBoost, ensemble methods, feature engineering, ROUGE and
  metric-driven evaluation.
- Languages: English and Turkish.

## Fit for roles

Kaan is a strong candidate for roles in AI / ML engineering, LLM
interpretability and safety research, applied research, and full-stack AI
product engineering. He combines research depth (understanding model internals,
not just calling APIs) with the ability to ship and deploy real systems. He
takes on broad, end-to-end responsibility, reasons from first principles thanks
to his physics background, and is a self-taught fast learner comfortable in
ambiguous, early-stage problems.
